subject: Life Skills
title: Carbon Monoxide: The Silent Killer
description: A quick, practical guide to Carbon Monoxide: The Silent Killer.

hook.text: A family felt dizzy and nauseous every winter evening. They blamed the flu. It was their furnace leaking CO.

buildup.text: Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless. You cannot detect it without a sensor. Symptoms mimic common illness.

discovery.text: CO binds to your blood 200 times more tightly than oxygen. At high levels, it can kill in minutes without warning.

twist.text: Generators, grills, and cars in garages are top sources. Running any fuel-burning device indoors is a serious risk.

climax.text: Install CO detectors on every level and near bedrooms. If the alarm sounds, evacuate immediately.

punchline.text: You cannot smell it, see it, or taste it. Detect it.

quiz.question: Why is carbon monoxide so dangerous?
options: It causes visible smoke that blocks vision
It is colorless and odorless, making it undetectable without a sensor
It only affects children and elderly people
